scores.evidence: Keyword search matters for error codes, feature names and SKUs, which embeddings handle poorly.
scores.rationale: Technical claims are accurate (hybrid search, cross-encoder reranking, re-index on embedding change), with minor issues such as LLM self-reported confidence and the vague cache invalidation.

scores.evidence: Non-goals for v1: account-specific actions (refunds, password resets), multi-turn troubleshooting flows
scores.rationale: Covers the core RAG needs with explicit non-goals and a buildable phased path; it leaves channel and platform open, and the 'right article in top 5' recall target assumes one-article mapping.

scores.evidence: Metadata filters: locale, product, and plan tier (if known from the session).
scores.rationale: The design is mostly consistent, but visibility is handled by exclusion at ingestion while plan tier filtering is session-dependent and only loosely tied to identity; some unowned data such as transcripts.

scores.evidence: Regression gate: run the eval in CI for any change to prompts, chunking, models or the index. Block a release if a metric drops.
scores.rationale: Golden set from tickets, LLM judge calibrated on human grading, CI gate, agent-assist pilot and online metrics are strong, but the targets are not justified beyond 'starting point' and the riskiest assumptions are not tested explicitly early.

scores.evidence: I don't know your stack, doc platform or volume yet, so this plan is vendor-neutral and lists its assumptions.
scores.rationale: Open questions and 'starting point' and 'est.' labels are good, but there is little sensitivity analysis, and numbers like 85% and 95% have no stated basis.

scores.evidence: Customers stuck in a bot loop | An always-visible "talk to a human" button, and auto-escalation after 2 failed turns
scores.rationale: Covers the main domain failures (hallucinated policy, stale docs, loops, injection, multilingual) with concrete mitigations, but lacks detail on partial ingestion failures, outage and fallback, and poisoned content.

scores.evidence: monitor ingestion lag and alert if an updated article isn't re-indexed within N minutes.
scores.rationale: Covers tracing, freshness alerting and weekly review, but has no rollback or deployment mechanism, index migration path, incident ownership or on-call.

scores.evidence: cache answers to frequent questions (invalidate when the source article changes), set token budgets, and rate-limit per session.
scores.rationale: Controls are named, but there is no cost-per-conversation estimate, no cost breakdown and no build-cost estimate.

scores.evidence: Changing the embedding model means a full re-index.
scores.rationale: It notes versioning and re-index cost and offers vendor-neutral store options, but it does not frame one-way versus reversible decisions or provide exit paths.

scores.evidence: Starting with agent assist (phase 2) is the lowest-risk path.
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate, with a phased rollout; query rewriting, reranking and hypothetical questions are included from the start without baseline evidence, though they are mostly standard and some are marked optional.

scores.evidence: Prototype | 2 wks | Ingestion, hybrid retrieval, generation with citations, offline eval passing the targets
scores.rationale: Phases are ordered sensibly with deliverables, but the plan is generic and vendor-neutral, offers little on concrete first steps or on what to do if targets are missed, and defers specifics to the open questions.

checklist.evidence: use a CMS webhook on publish, update or delete, plus a nightly full reconciliation. Deletes must remove chunks from the index.
Chunk by document structure (H2/H3 sections), not fixed tokens.
Golden dataset (200–500 questions): take them from real historical tickets and chat logs
If the context doesn't contain the answer, say so and offer escalation.
create a ticket with the full transcript, the retrieved articles, and the bot's draft answer
treat retrieved text and user text as data, not instructions. The bot should have no tools that can take actions in v1.
Exclude internal-only articles, drafts, and anything with agent-only notes. Filter on article visibility metadata.
redact card numbers, SSNs and similar data before logging. Set a log retention policy.
Non-goals for v1: account-specific actions (refunds, password resets)
Content-gap report: list questions with low retrieval scores or that escalated, clustered by topic.
cache answers to frequent questions (invalidate when the source article changes), set token budgets, and rate-limit per session.

traps.evidence: Answer only from the provided context.
Exclude internal-only articles, drafts, and anything with agent-only notes.
Regression gate: run the eval in CI for any change to prompts, chunking, models or the index.
Query rewriting: turn the conversation into one self-contained search query

note: Solid, sensible vendor-neutral RAG plan with strong eval and a safe agent-assist rollout; weak on retrieval-time entitlements, cost estimates, data-protection detail and operational rollback.
